c1-dc2-guard-real.title: CC1: permanent DC2 guard is real
c1-dc2-guard-real.imperative: Read test_handoff_advance_at_hard_with_no_refresh_request_closes_and_freshens_digest. Verify it pins fill>=hard AND no pending refresh-request anywhere in the spine, asserted inside the test body. A pending request anywhere = BLOCK.
c1-dc2-guard-real.finding: PASS -- the claim is TRUE and I verified it three ways. (1) Read the test (tests/test_checklist_engine.py:3497-3517): line 3507 asserts _refresh_requests_anywhere(cl)==[] BEFORE the advance and line 3517 asserts it again AFTER; line 3510 asserts E._read_gauge(Path('.')).fill_fraction >= self.hard INSIDE the patch context. Both preconditions are in the test body, not the fixture comment. (2) Audited the helper at :3234 against the engine predicate it must dominate: _refresh_requests_anywhere walks every task's evidence and does NOT filter superseded, while has_pending_refresh_request (engine :1155) walks the same task-evidence domain and DOES skip superseded. The helper is therefore a strict SUPERSET of everything that could lift the guard -- it cannot miss a lifting request. (3) Falsified directly: ran the NEW test file against the PRE-change engine (git show 38f0b448^:scripts/checklist_engine.py in an isolated tree) and this exact test FAILS, for the right reason -- the pre-#467 dispatch raises 'advancing is blocked until you request a refresh'. A second independent guard exists at the real-file tier (TripRealGaugeFileWiring::test_handoff_fresh_hard_gauge_never_refuses_the_closing_advance) driving a REAL gauge.json through main(); it too is red pre-change (AssertionError: 1 != 0).

c9-docs.title: CC9: CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md describes shipped behaviour
c9-docs.imperative: Read the shipped Trip section and the start/advance/reopen verb rows; verify they match shipped code, not the old refusal. Also judge the new advisory prose against the FIXED constraints.
c9-docs.finding: PASS with one non-blocking accuracy nit. Read the shipped Trip section and the three verb rows and checked each claim against source: the section title changed from 'HARD refuse-advance' to 'HARD guards the BEGIN verbs'; it names TRIP_HARD_GUARDED_VERBS, states that HARD does NOT refuse advance and that resume is likewise unguarded, documents the no-silent-close rule with the #431 mechanism, states 'HARD means wrap up, never you are unsafe', and describes the require_why seam. The start and reopen rows say 'Refused at/over the Trip HARD threshold', the advance row says 'Never refused by Trip HARD'. All true of the shipped code. PROSE CHECK against the FIXED group -- I read the shipped strings, not the tests: the HARD advisory is 'your instruction has changed. You have taken this as far as this context can carry it -- now close THIS gate carrying your handoff (advance <g> --why "<understanding>"), request a refresh, and stop. A fresh agent picks up from your DIGEST; do not begin work at another gate.' That reads as a changed instruction, contains no alarm word, does not claim advance is blocked, and tells the agent the one thing to do; the test pins the absence of BLOCKED/unsafe/runaway/lost. A missing reading still forces nothing, and the reading is pushed by the engine on the verb, never fetched. NON-BLOCKING NIT: the new sentence 'A refusal is raised before the liveness stamp, so it never refreshes the lease and never mutates state' is true of the start/reopen guard (I measured: only the refusals counter moves, and last_heartbeat is unchanged) but the 'never mutates state' half is not strictly true of the no-silent-close refusal inside advance, which lands AFTER the postcondition check has stamped satisfied and attached command-output. I confirmed against the pre-change engine that this is long-standing behaviour for any post-postcondition refusal, not a #467 regression -- but the doc sentence is new and now spans both refusals, so it slightly overstates. Suggest scoping it to the pre-verb guard.

consolidation.summary: APPROVE, zero blocking findings. All nine close criteria PASS, each verified against the world rather than the report. The decisive check (c1) holds: the permanent DC2 guard asserts BOTH preconditions inside its own body -- _refresh_requests_anywhere(cl)==[] before AND after, and fill>=hard inside the patch -- and the helper is a strict superset of the engine predicate that would lift the guard, so it cannot miss one. I falsified rather than confirmed: running the NEW test file against the PRE-change engine in an isolated tree reddens 16 of the 25 selector tests, including both DC2 guards at the mocked and real-file tiers; the 9 that stay green are all declared falsifiable-half/fail-safe companions, none dressed as a guard. Four mutations re-run (M3, M5, M2, M8 -- chosen as the most falsifiable, not the first two): counts 1/6/3/5 and the exact failure SETS matched the log with zero discrepancy, off a reproduced 416-passed baseline. Both claims I was told to attack survive: M11's declared limitation is honest -- my own two narrower candidates still redden 37 and 23 -- and the -1 subtest is GONE now that the gate is committed (1815 passed / 2 skipped / 683 subtests, exit 0, mechanically-derived failure distribution empty). Four adversarial probes through main() with a real gauge: the refusal does not refresh the lease and the begin-guard mutates nothing but a counter; why_exempt suspension actually WRITES the why_trail record; reopen refused / resume allowed; and the full #431 scenario side by side against the pre-change engine -- old: rc 1, gate stuck, digest stays PRE-TRIP; new: rc 0, gate closes, digest FRESH, and beginning the next gate over the line is still refused. Per inherited crew doctrine I EXECUTED the engine's emitted advice verbatim across all four dimensions and it released the guard every time. Non-blocking: GLOSSARY.md:13 still teaches 'HARD blocks advance' (out of scope, correctly escalated, must-fix before the epic closes); no test executes the emitted hint, so #467(d)'s guard is a string match; three Fowler smells flagged; one doc sentence slightly overstates 'never mutates state'.

CONFIRMED by my own blast-radius grep. OUT of this gate's allowed scope (which named CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md's Trip section only) and correctly escalated rather than edited, so NOT blocking for g2. Must-fix before epic #418 closes: one line, one file.

No test EXECUTES the emitted refresh hint -- the permanent guard for #467(d) is an assertEqual on the rendered string. Inherited crew doctrine says string-matching generated advice is not evidence; #467(d) IS that failure mode. Shipped behaviour is CORRECT (my PROBE E shlex-splits the engine's own emitted string and runs it across refusal/advisory surface x live-why-record/fallback -- releases in all four), but a future change that preserves the string and breaks the execution stays green. Recommend one execute-the-hint test.
